references.note: Approved style anchor: reuse its steep overhead three-quarter camera, matte sculpted miniature finish, thin charcoal-brown physical disc and muted bronze-grey bevel at exactly that lightness. Do not copy its species, body plan, pose or tail.
Native species only: a heavy brown hare-like rabbit with long ears and powerful haunches. Ignore the native camera and lighting.

Existing mapped giant brown rat. The rabbit shares its warm brown value range, so it must never be readable as a large rat: no long bare tail, no pointed rat muzzle, no low horizontal four-footed bar silhouette.

prompt_fields.subject: One heavy giant rabbit crouched low on the disc in a three-quarter front view, head toward the lower left. Thick loaf-shaped body, very large muscular hind haunches folded under it, short tucked forelegs, blunt rounded muzzle with a cleft lip and short whiskers, and two long narrow upright ears rising well above the head as a tall parallel pair with a visible gap of dark disc between them. Only a small round puff of a tail, tight against the rump.
prompt_fields.contrast: The mapped giant brown rat is a long low horizontal four-footed bar with a pointed muzzle, small ears and a long thick bare tail arcing across the disc. This rabbit must differ in at least two dimensions: (1) silhouette — a tall compact hunched mass whose outline is dominated by two long narrow vertical ears and a huge rounded haunch, with no long tail anywhere; (2) value pattern — a bright lit crown and shoulder plane over one very dark deep haunch/chest core and pale ear interiors, instead of the rat art's single even body mass. It must also not be confused with the giant mice in the same batch: the mice sit upright with two round disc ears and a long thin tail, the rabbit crouches with two long blade ears and no visible tail. Distinction must survive grayscale at 48px.
prompt_fields.composition: One entire animal on one disc, steep overhead three-quarter view. Ear tips, forefeet, hind feet and rump all stay inside the disc with clear margin; the outer sixth of the disc radius stays bare base plate. Lean the ear pair slightly away from the upper-right rank corner and keep the upper-left interaction corner clear. Keep the two ears separated by a readable dark gap so they do not fuse into one blob at 48px.
prompt_fields.palette: Warm umber and russet-brown dorsal fur with a paler oatmeal-tan chest and cheek, dusty pink-grey inner ear lining, dark liquid eye, dark nose, and a compact warm-grey contact shadow. Matte painted fur, no glow, no effect, no grass or burrow.

references.note: Approved style anchor: reuse its steep overhead three-quarter camera, matte sculpted miniature finish, thin charcoal-brown physical disc and muted bronze-grey bevel at exactly that lightness. Do not copy its species, body plan, pose or tail.

Native species only: a rat whose back and flanks carry a crust of pale angular crystal shards. Ignore the native camera and the engine blue tint; the crystals are ordinary matte mineral, not a light source.

Existing mapped giant white rat. This crystal rat is also pale, so it must never be readable as the white rat: break the smooth back line with hard angular crystal ridges and keep the fur clearly darker than the crystals.

prompt_fields.subject: One large adult rat seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle, walking to the right with its head lowered at the lower right and haunches raised at the upper left. Long pointed muzzle, rounded ears, four clawed feet and a long bare tail curving down and back to the left. A dense crust of pale angular crystal shards grows out of the fur along the whole spine and over both shoulders and the rump, forming a jagged sawtooth ridge that clearly breaks the smooth outline of the back. A few smaller facets sit on the flanks. The crystals are hard, faceted and matte-translucent, like rose quartz grown through fur; they are armour, not light.
prompt_fields.contrast: The mapped giant white rat is one smooth broad ivory mass with a raised forebody and a soft rounded back line; the mapped giant grey rat is a smooth low slate bar. This crystal rat must differ in at least two dimensions: (1) silhouette — the top edge of the body is a hard jagged crystalline sawtooth ridge instead of a smooth fur curve; (2) value pattern — dark dusty mauve-grey fur carrying a chain of small hard-edged bright facets with sharp cast shadows, a high-frequency light-on-dark pattern that no other rat in the set has. Hue is a third, secondary cue only. Do not reduce this to a recoloured white rat. Distinction must survive grayscale at 48px.
prompt_fields.composition: One entire animal on one disc, steep overhead three-quarter view. Muzzle, ears, all four feet, the whole tail and every crystal tip stay inside the disc with clear margin; the outer sixth of the disc radius stays bare base plate. Keep the head out of the upper-right rank corner and the upper-left interaction corner clear. Leave a readable wedge of dark disc between the tail and the body. Keep the crystal ridge coarse enough that it still reads as spikes at 48px, not as noise.
prompt_fields.palette: Dusty mauve-grey and dark taupe fur, pale rose-quartz and bone-pink crystal facets with cool grey shadow planes, bare pink-grey tail, feet and ears, dark eyes. Matte mineral, no emitted light, no glow, no sparkle stars, no blue engine tint, no effect.
